change.purpose: Select an explicit documented software backend to isolate the observed adaptive Lavapipe/SwANGLE selection. This does not establish which component caused SIGSEGV or prove the new mode will cure it.

primarySources.finding: The current documentation lists software as an adaptive software selector and swiftshader as a supported software option for GLES and Vulkan. It also lists lavapipe and swangle separately; swiftshader_indirect was deprecated in 36.4.9.

The documented -feature -Vulkan argument disables Vulkan. It is deliberately omitted here to retain that coverage and avoid adding a second experiment. The page also documents -gpu swiftshader as a graphics troubleshooting option.
The installed 37.2.13 already includes the Oct 28, 2026 fix for a host GLES resource leak after guest process exit. Recent macOS-specific fixes do not establish a remedy for this Linux host SIGSEGV.
No positively matching fix for the observed Linux host crash was identified in the reviewed 37.x stable/canary issue list; no upgrade or downgrade is proposed.

findings: emugl_config.cpp separates Vulkan and GLES selection. The reviewed Linux explicit swiftshader path selects the SwiftShader Vulkan ICD and GLES library; the Lavapipe path defaults GLES to SwANGLE. The next runtime logs must verify the installed binary actually makes the expected selection.

The reviewed code emits the same selected-mode diagnostic seen in the retained failed-run log. The source also contains a GLES 3.1/API 35 compatibility condition, so documented mode support is not treated as complete feature-equivalence proof for the unchanged API 35 test image.
The retrieved public branch commit is not established as the exact source revision of installed build 16740729. No source-based installed-binary identity claim is made.

diagnosticCollection.mode: best effort after existing emulator stop/wait in the existing EXIT cleanup
runBinding: Linux CI QA environment and numeric workflow run identity
Actual launched PID and nanosecond launch marker passed by the runner
One current regular emulator.log with one version and one Crashpad marker matching that PID
Exact /tmp/android-<current-user>/emu-crash-<logged-version>.db path, checked through no-follow directory descriptors
Only regular single-link current-user files modified within the current launch/collection window
pathSafety: No /tmp sweep, arbitrary path, symlink traversal, foreign owner, hardlink, FIFO or device copying
Fresh output directory required; existing output or symlink is rejected
Source files are opened relative to checked directory descriptors; before/after descriptor metadata detects observed mutation
Incomplete copies are removed and never marked complete; source files are not modified or deleted
diagnosticCollection.manifest: Records copied/skipped files, hashes, bounds, PID, current run/log binding and the pre-cleanup shell status; missing or rejected diagnostics do not change the acceptance gate.
coverageLimits: The store name is version/user based, not per-process. Binding uses the current process marker and file modification window; it is not proof of the producer of every byte.
Crashpad may have no complete current dump, and size/time limits can intentionally omit data. Missing diagnostics never count as acceptance.
gateExitCode records the status observed on entry to EXIT cleanup. Under cancellation it is not necessarily the final signal/workflow result and must never be used as the acceptance verdict.
An external termination may stop collection before a manifest is written. Existing mandatory flow/JUnit/decoder/full-app results and workflow conclusion remain authoritative.
additionalVersionHelpEvidence: existing emulator.log with actual backend selection
